rows: The small tornado was on the ground for less than a minute and remained over open country. No damage and no injuries were reported. The path length and path width were estimated.
Hail was reportedly covering the ground.
Reported near Dunn Road and State Highway 102.
Reported along Farm to Market Road 297.
Time of the hail was estimated.
Reported along Farm to Market Road 1727 in southern Dallam County.
The general public reported that the hail ranged in size from golf balls to baseballs.

The tornado touched down three miles east northeast of Ware at 1952 CST and remained over open country. The tornado was on the ground for about one half mile with a maximum path width of twenty-five yards. The tornado dissipated at 1953 CST. No damage or injuries were reported.

The tornado touched down eight miles west of Conlen at 2030 CST and remained over open country. The tornado was on the ground for about four miles with a maximum path width of twenty-five yards. The tornado dissipated at 2042 CST. No damage or injuries were reported.
The local law enforcement reported that thunderstorm wind gusts downed trees and power lines on the west and north sides of Texline.
A trained National Weather Service storm spotter observed power flashes, however no damages or injuries were reported.
Local law enforcement officials estimated the thunderstorm wind gust about one mile north of Dalhart Texas. There were no reports of damages or injuries.

Local law enforcement officials estimated the thunderstorm wind gust and also reported that there were several power lines blown down around the city of Dalhart Texas. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.

Half dollar size hail was reported in Kerrick, 15 miles northwest of Stratford.
Tree limbs 10 inches in diameter were blown down.

Hail up to the size of half dollars fell 4 miles east of Dalhart.
Wind gusts estimated between 60 and 70 mph were reported 4 miles east-northeast of Dalhart.
A storm chaser estimated a wind gust of 65 mph 13 miles northeast of Ware.

Ping pong ball size hail was reported at Conlen Airport.
A grain elevator was blown over and blocking Highway 87 near Pollard Road. Further south in Dallam County some irrigation pivots were blown over.

A grain bin was damaged and irrigation pivots flipped near Highway 102 and McAdams, 17 miles south-southeast of Texline.

Damage from this short track, small tornado included a destroyed grain silo, tree damage, a flipped center pivot irrigation system and minor roof damage to a farm house. This resulted in EF-1 rating with estimated peak winds of 87 mph.

This tornado resulted in flattened grass, a flipped center pivot irrigation system and a small trailer flipped over in a field. This was consistent with EF-0 damage and estimated peak winds of 80 mph.
Quarter size hail increased to golf ball size at 6th and Keeler in Dalhart.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell 4 miles east-northeast of Dalhart.
Tree branches 4-6 inch diameter downed by strong wind gusts.
Pea to quarter size hail covering the ground with heavy rain for 20 minutes south-southeast of Texline.
Hail up to the size of half dollars 3 miles northwest of Dalhart on us 87.
Trailer was destroyed NW of Dalhart.
Center pivot irrigation system flipped at the intersection of HWY 87 and 102.
Hail covering the roadways at the intersection of FM 1727 and HWY 87 north.
Late report of thunderstorm wind gusts estimated up to 60 MPH.
Trained spotter estimated wind gust of 60 MPH.
Five power poles down in a row.

A few tree limbs 9 to 16 inches in diameter were blown down.
Delayed report. A few tree limbs down in downtown Dalhart. Time estimated based on KDHT wind observation.

Storm chaser reported 1-2 inch diameter hail in and around Dalhart to around 5 miles north of town. Some minor accumulating hail was reported on highway 385, about 4 miles north of the city as well.
Report received of 1 to 1.5 inch hail falling for around 2 minutes.
Wind driven hail caused extensive damage to house and trees. All windows on north side of house were blown out.
Hail caused broken windows and hail damage.
Hail up to the 4 in diameter reported 22 miles NNE of Ware reported by the public. Hail up to 1.75 reported 7 miles N of Conlen by a trained spotter.
This tornado touched down in an open field and was documented by|several storm spotters and chasers. It did not cause any damage|and was given an EFU damage rating.
A large tree was blown over onto a house. A trained spotter had collected a report from the resident of this home. Resident said there was no damage on the inside of the house.
Several tree limbs, 1 to 2 in diameter, were blown down by thunderstorm wind gusts.
A swath of quarter size hail fell in Texline and just to the east of town.
Hail ranging from quarter to baseball size fell across and just to the south of Texline.
Hail up to two inches in diameter fell across Dalhart.
This mesonet showed additional gusts of 58-60mph several | times from 1737CDT through 1750CDT.
Video that was posted on social media shows a grain silo destroyed and laying across the south bound lane of Highway 87.
First wind gust was at 1749CDT was 60 mph. The max wind gust of 61 mph occurred at 1751CDT. Severe wind gusts persisted for 6 minutes from 1749 through 1755CDT.
The roof of a grain silo was ripped off and the west side wall of the silo was caved in.

This tornado remained in open grassland causing no damage. The only damage indicator it crossed was a powerline on E0330 Road which was not damaged. It did result in flattened grass along a portion of its track. The total track length was around 9.4 miles.
Chasers documented a brief and weak touchdown in open field south of Perico. No other damage was noted.
The tornado touched down in rural southwest Dallam County and it destroyed a barn south of FM 1727. The estimated maximum wind speed was 95mph.

Strong winds and hail occurred over large area just west of Dalhart to the state line, generally extending from around Highway 87 to Highway 54. This impacted many farms and there was damage to crops throughout the area. This included some fields that were completely flattened an…
First severe wind gust occurred at 1813 CDT and last severe wind gust occurred at 1815 CDT at the mesonet site two miles north of Texline.
Hail fell to the east of Dalhart. The sizes were mostly nickel-sized but there were some hailstones the size of golf balls mixed in as well.
A swath of small hail occurred across portions of Dallam County. Hail covered the ground to the northeast of Dalhart, with stones that ranged from pea to penny size.
A supercell thunderstorm moved across Texline and brought large hail of 2.25 inches to 2.5 inches across the city.
A 71mph wind gust was measured at the mesonet site located two miles north of Texline. This gust was followed by a 65mph and 60mph wind gust as well.
